newsitem.title: UK: Frontline says put to make $1mln profit.
newsitem.headline: Frontline says put to make $1mln profit.

text.p: Newly Oslo-listed tanker operator Frontline Ltd said Tuesday that investor Goldtec has asked it to exercise a put option in its shares.
The put will involve the sale of just over 1.1 million Frontline shares at an average price of 28.60 Norwegian crowns per share, Frontline said.

Frontline said any profit arising from the difference between the sales price received for the shares and the minimum sales price of 23.06 Swedish crowns per share, plus 5.8 percent annual interest from July 1, 1997, will belong to Frontline Ltd. Until last week the company was listed in Stockholm.
"The profit arising from this sale estimated at $1 million will be booked in Frontline Ltd's third quarter results," the company said.

Frontline said the move resulted from a call agreement with Swedish freight forwarding group BTL and Goldtec allowing Frontline to order the sale of up to 2,225,000 Frontline Ltd shares each from BTL and Goldtec to any buyer that Frontline Ltd may advise.
BTL and Goldtec also had an option to put 1,112,500 of the same shares to Frontline Ltd at the same price as in the call arrangement.
